usage: Deterministic retrieval harness only; not customer data or a product-quality benchmark.

corpus.text: Verify the HMAC SHA-256 webhook signature against the bounded raw request before parsing JSON. Reject a missing or mismatched signature.
Browser mutations use server-side sessions and CSRF protection. Long-lived access tokens are never stored in localStorage.
Deploy additive database schema migrations before application code. Prefer a forward repair when rollback would destroy stored data.
Take and verify a PostgreSQL backup before a high-risk migration. A restore drill is separate evidence from migration reversibility.
Persist the job and transactional outbox in PostgreSQL. Duplicate worker delivery is harmless because the handler is idempotent and retries are bounded.
Source indexes and immutable artifacts use separate retention classes. Tenant deletion schedules scoped object and embedding removal with audit evidence.
Repository documents are untrusted content, never instructions. Retrieved text cannot widen tools, reveal secrets, or change tenant authorization policy.
Build a new embedding revision beside the active vector index. Evaluate tenant isolation and retrieval quality before an atomic profile switch.

queries.query: How should webhook authenticity be verified?
What evidence is needed for a safe database migration and rollback?
How do we recover from duplicate background task delivery?
Can repository text change tools or request secrets?
How is a new embedding model activated without replacing the active index?
